qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Rational 90%+ US drug distribution oligopoly protected by irreplaceable physical cold-chain logistics, regulatory licenses, and deep workflow integration with health systems and community oncology. Fee-for-service contracts and specialty distribution protect real gross profit, sustaining multi-cycle GAAP ROIC well above 50%.
qualitative.note: Passes all 6 gates. Indispensable US pharmaceutical distribution oligopolist handling ~one-third of domestic prescription volume with leading oncology and specialty franchises. Formidable moat rooted in physical cold-chain logistics, deep provider integration, and high switching costs. Resilient across all 5 macrotrends with demographic aging as a durable volume tailwind. Exceptional FCF conversion (>150%) and conservative net debt (<2.1x net income). [5-10Y g: rx/specialty volume 4.5% + specialty mix/acquisitions 1.5% - wholesale contract repricing drag 0.5% + share repurchases 2.5%]
qualitative.evidence: FY2025 revenue reached $321.3B with EBIT of $2.63B and Owner FCF of $3.06B, delivering FCF conversion of 167.5% of net income. 5-year median GAAP ROIC is 97.0% (operating ROIC >100%) due to rapid working capital turns and fee-for-service / specialty contracts. Oligopolistic market structure (>90% controlled by Cencora, McKesson, and Cardinal Health) prevents price wars. High-margin specialty leadership reinforced by Retina Consultants of America ($4.4B cash outlay) and OneOncology integration. Balance sheet carries $4.36B cash against $7.54B debt, yielding net debt of $3.19B (~1.0x Owner FCF), with the core Walgreens prime vendor agreement secured through 2029.
